title: Active Support & Railtie
intro: Active Support is Rails' utility belt — the extensions to Ruby's standard library that make blank?, present?, try, deep_merge, and in_time_zone available everywhere. It also provides the Concern module that powers the include pattern used throughout Rails itself. This page covers the topics that appear in intermediate interviews: ActiveSupport::Concern and why it replaces the base.included boilerplate, the time zone trap (Time.now vs Time.current, and why you must always use the latter in Rails apps with global time zones), the delegate macro, class_attribute vs cattr_accessor, and how Railtie hooks gems into Rails' initialization lifecycle. The time zone question catches many engineers — storing and displaying times incorrectly is a real production bug.
